meta.title: Multi-Channel Invitation and Reminders: refused for a user without the Buyer role
gaps: Sign in as a user without the Buyer role and verify Multi-Channel Invitation and Reminders is refused or absent, then repeat as a Buyer and verify it is available.
Determine whether the tenant's RBAC configuration intentionally grants this action to roles other than Buyer.
Execute and verify the full multi-channel notification and automated reminder workflow.
warnings: can only test part of this — no step for: Sign in as a user without the Buyer role and verify Multi-Channel Invitation and Reminders is refused or absent, then repeat as a Buyer and verify it is available.; Determine whether the tenant's RBAC configuration intentionally grants this action to roles other than Buyer.; Execute and verify the full multi-channel notification and automated reminder workflow.

steps.note: Open an existing event where the reminder action can be inspected.
Check whether the event menu offers the reminder action, which is the closest catalog-level availability check.
Open the reminder drawer to inspect the available reminder workflow.
Assert that the Send Reminders drawer opened with its expected offer-submission content.

args.need: sign in as the non-Buyer user and the Buyer user on the same tenant, verify Multi-Channel Invitation and Reminders is refused or absent for the non-Buyer and available for the Buyer, and report any intentional RBAC configuration granting it to other roles

steps.note: Role-specific authentication, permission comparison, tenant RBAC interpretation, and the complete multi-channel reminder action require user access and verification outside the catalog.
Final assertion that the reminder workflow screen remains observable after the role comparison.
